A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study, with matching authors, title, task families and core experiments. The complete main texts and appendices are readable, supporting comparison despite substantial restructuring and substantive revisions.

before.justification: V1 reports original model evaluations, fine-tuning experiments, attention measurements, architecture comparisons and failure analyses in Sections 5–6 and the appendices.

after.justification: V2 retains original benchmark, fine-tuning and mechanistic results and additionally reports attention-window measurements and individual-run accuracies in Appendices E and F.

M1.justification: The core CoT, BFS tool-delegation and Llama fine-tuning procedures remain. V2's incremental SSJ Algorithm 2 already appears as Algorithm 3 in v1; consolidating the conflicting metric descriptions does not establish a new model or reasoning algorithm.

E1.justification: All eight task families and three real-world source benchmarks remain. ArithChain's specified operators narrow from addition, subtraction, multiplication and division in v1 Section 28.1.3 to the first three operations, with b coprime to p, in v2 Table 10. Modular arithmetic itself was already documented in v1's appendix.

E2.justification: V2 removes the evaluated T5-Large, BART-Large and Flan-T5-XL encoder–decoder comparisons from v1 Tables 12 and 18, and the GPT-4o Best-of-10 comparison reported in v1's cost analyses. The twelve primary models remain, but entire alternative-architecture and repeated-sampling comparisons disappear.

E3.justification: V2 replaces the claimed full model-task-condition grid with 173 populated cells and restricts C5 to Llama-3.1-8B on PermutationProbe. Its instance generator uses rejection sampling of uniform permutations instead of random swap sequences, and attention reporting changes from normalized entropy to raw bits, with revised layer groupings. These are substantive reported protocol revisions; the PDFs do not establish that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: V2 newly reports effective attention-window scaling across context lengths and an analysis of run-level variance. It removes cross-model failure correlations, encoder–decoder and cost/carbon analyses, lagged error autocorrelations, SSJ extraction validation, and the 4K/2K truncation results. The main failure taxonomy, training-distribution ablation and 128K–8K truncation analysis remain.

E5.justification: V2 retains three-run standard deviations but withdraws the bootstrap/BCa methodology, Bayes factors and power guarantees, and removes several correlation confidence intervals. Appendices F and J explain that seeds label nondeterministic repetitions rather than independent samples, specify per-instance likelihood-ratio tests, and qualify run-level equivalence claims. This substantially changes the statistical support without establishing additional runs.

E6.justification: Many primary scores remain, but substantial entries change or disappear. Llama's depth-21–30 baseline/fine-tuned accuracies change from 38.6/40.2 to 27.7/29.3 (v1 Table 16; v2 Table 24), and GPT-4o C2 at that depth changes from 48.3 to 51.4 (v1 Table 35; v2 Table 22). Most C5 entries are removed, attention-window and individual-run results are added, and model selection now favors the quadratic model instead of the context-dependent model.

T1.justification: The capacity bound changes from H log(L/H) sqrt(dh) to H log(L) sqrt(dh) and is restricted to a single-layer read channel; its assumptions and lower-bound construction also change. V2 corrects the product-bound premise, distinguishes error-free traces from final-state correctness, and adds the large-Leff saturation limit. V1's universal fine-tuning theorem and architecture-scaling corollary become empirical statements.

C1.justification: The abstract and contributions retreat from SSJ as a discriminator of failure causes, cross-model correlation as architectural proof, and fine-tuning as confirmation of a universal ceiling. V2 emphasizes non-binding total capacity, an empirical 50%-accuracy horizon and qualified support for architectural limitations. The conclusion also drops the cost-efficiency contribution.

C2.justification: V2 treats entropy correlations as association, acknowledges shared-depth confounding and unmeasured anchor-attention decay, and interprets the horizon as a reliability threshold rather than a neural–tool crossover. New qualifications address parameter identifiability, architecture/size confounding, output truncation, contamination, SSJ's diagnostic limits and weak run-level inference. These materially narrow the causal and deployment interpretations.

D1.justification: V2 adds licensing and subset-reconstruction information, top-p and reasoning-effort settings, system-prompt and grading details, and batching, concurrency and runtime-accounting disclosures. It also revises the stated o3 version identifier. These refine an already detailed reproducibility record; the exact condition prompts, principal training settings, hardware and code address largely remain.

R1.justification: V2 fundamentally revises its positioning against Wu et al.: the earlier preference-bias account and attributed greater-than-30% recovery prediction become a sub-task-difficulty account, with thresholds explicitly identified as this paper's operationalization. It also qualifies the relevance of Gong and Zhang's N-back evidence. Goldfeld and Polyanskiy is added, while works including Deb and Ogunfunmi and Lewandowsky and Bauch are removed.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, theoretical explanations, related work, discussion and conclusion undergo extensive rewriting. V1's fragmented appendices A–Z and 27–33 are consolidated into A–J, bringing notation forward and grouping proofs, specifications, protocols, results and statistical discussion. This is substantial narrative reorganization beyond the scientific changes.

P2.justification: Table 2 is rebuilt around open-weight models and C2; notation and task specifications are consolidated into tables, and individual-run accuracies receive a new table. Numerous architecture, correlation and cost displays are removed. Figure 1 is redrawn with a fitted-model label and depth-dependent tool scores already available in v1's appendix; the normalized-entropy figure disappears, while fine-tuning and SSJ plots are relocated and recaptioned.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially improves scientific defensibility by correcting product-bound logic, separating error-free-trace bounds from final-answer accuracy, withdrawing the universal fine-tuning theorem, and acknowledging the limitations of three nondeterministic runs. It also makes assumptions and empirical fitting explicit and revises the attribution of competing predictions. Removed comparisons reduce breadth, and unexplained numerical revisions and inconsistent SSJ statements remain, but the central claims are substantially better calibrated to the evidence.
